From adb25a46dc0a43173f5ea5f5f58fc8ba28970c7c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shivani Gupta <shivani07g@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jan 2026 00:59:05 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net/sched: act_api: avoid dereferencing ERR_PTR in
 tcf_idrinfo_destroy

syzbot reported a crash in tc_act_in_hw() during netns teardown where
tcf_idrinfo_destroy() passed an ERR_PTR(-EBUSY) value as a tc_action
pointer, leading to an invalid dereference.

Guard against ERR_PTR entries when iterating the action IDR so teardown
does not call tc_act_in_hw() on an error pointer.

Fixes: 84a7d6797e6a ("net/sched: acp_api: no longer acquire RTNL in tc_action_net_exit()")
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=8f1c492ffa4644ff3826
Reported-by: syzbot+8f1c492ffa4644ff3826@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=8f1c492ffa4644ff3826
Signed-off-by: Shivani Gupta <shivani07g@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260105005905.243423-1-shivani07g@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/sched/act_api.c b/net/sched/act_api.c
index ff6be5cfe2b0..e1ab0faeb811 100644
--- a/net/sched/act_api.c
+++ b/net/sched/act_api.c
@@ -940,6 +940,8 @@ void tcf_idrinfo_destroy(const struct tc_action_ops *ops,
 	int ret;
 
 	idr_for_each_entry_ul(idr, p, tmp, id) {
+		if (IS_ERR(p))
+			continue;
 		if (tc_act_in_hw(p) && !mutex_taken) {
 			rtnl_lock();
 			mutex_taken = true;
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

- **File: `net/sched/act_api.c`**  
  In the `tcf_idrinfo_destroy` function, added a guard check `if (IS_ERR(p)) continue;` inside the IDR iteration loop (`idr_for_each_entry_ul`). This prevents calling `tc_act_in_hw(p)` on an error pointer (e.g., `ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)`) that could have been stored in the IDR during concurrent operations, thereby avoiding a null/invalid dereference crash during network namespace teardown.

- **Relationship**  
  The single change directly addresses the root cause of the bug: the iteration over the action IDR could encounter `ERR_PTR` values passed as `tc_action` pointers. By skipping such entries, the fix ensures that only valid action pointers are passed to `tc_act_in_hw()`, preventing the invalid dereference reported by syzbot. This is a minimal, targeted fix that preserves the existing logic for valid entries.

Root cause:
During netns teardown, `tcf_idrinfo_destroy()` iterates over the action IDR using `idr_for_each_entry_ul`, which can yield `ERR_PTR` values (e.g., `-EBUSY`) from concurrent operations. The function then calls `tc_act_in_hw()` on such error pointers without checking `IS_ERR`, causing an invalid dereference and crash.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
idr_for_each_entry_ul(idr, p, tmp, id) {
	if (tc_act_in_hw(p) && !mutex_taken) {
Reason: The loop may retrieve ERR_PTR values from the IDR due to concurrent operations, and then passes the error pointer directly to tc_act_in_hw(p) without checking IS_ERR(p), causing invalid memory dereference.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+		if (IS_ERR(p))
+			continue;
Reason: By checking IS_ERR(p) before using p, the iteration safely skips error pointers, preventing dereference of invalid pointers in tc_act_in_hw() and other subsequent calls.
